title: Quasi-coherent modules detect Tor amplitude on affine schemes
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], and let $a\le b$ be integers. Suppose $H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every integer $i<a$ or $b<i$, with vanishing as in [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. Then the same vanishing holds for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$, without a quasi-coherence hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, affine paragraph using Tag 06Z0 and Tag 08E9; Tag 08E9 proof using the bounded flat-model criterion of Tag 0654

proof.text: Use exists_affine_module_complex_representative to write E as Q of termwise tilde followed by restriction along X.toSpecΓ. The public theorem tilde_preserves_finite_limits gives exactness of tilde together with its left adjunction. Restriction is exact, and its composite with restriction along X.isoSpec.inv is naturally the identity, so it is faithful. Tilde is fully faithful. Both exact functors therefore commute with complex homology, and their composite reflects zero objects by injectivity on morphisms.

Resolve the module complex M by a K-flat complex P. For every module N, restriction of tilde N is quasi-coherent. Apply the hypothesis to this sheaf and use the existing tensor_vanishes_iff helper from TorAmplitudeOpenLocal. The two single-complex comparison isomorphisms and affine_derivedTensor_chart_comparison identify the tested tensor with Q of restriction of tilde Tot(P tensor N[0]). Exactness of tilde and restriction identifies its homology with restriction of tilde of the module homology. Faithfulness reflects zero identity maps. The K-flat module derived-tensor model and the isGE_iff/isLE_iff criteria then give Tor amplitude [a,b] for Q(M).

Apply module_torAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flat_model to obtain a module complex B of flat modules with zero terms outside [a,b] and a derived isomorphism Q(M) to Q(B). Map this isomorphism through the exact derived tilde and restriction functors, using their localization factorization isomorphisms, to obtain Q of restriction of tilde B isomorphic to E. The bounded-above flat K-flat theorem, isKFlat_tilde and isKFlat_restrict show that this is a K-flat representative.

For an arbitrary sheaf G and i outside [a,b], use mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso to identify the total tensor of this representative with G[0] with the termwise tensorRight G complex. Tilde, restriction and tensorRight G preserve zero objects, so its degree i term is zero. ExactAt.of_isZero and ExactAt.isZero_homology give zero homology. The representative, its K-flatness and its isomorphism to E witness the required vanishing predicate.

lean.statement:
theorem affineQCoh_torAmplitude_detection (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X E)
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (h : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace),
      F.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i →
        schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes X E F i) :
    ∀ G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace),
      ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes X E G i
